critic_summary: The loop-1 method (4-step linear single-pass) allowed the researcher to commit to a key quantitative parameter (flow_threshold=0.6) derived from an explicitly stated false assumption (uniform trade-arrival density inside the 10s window) without ever confronting that assumption with the training data; the researcher flagged it as a concern in NOTES.md but the method gave no mechanism to act on it, and the backtest regressed -15.19% vs base with trade_count nearly unchanged (-0.22%) — i.e. the gate moved which orders it skipped, not how many, on the basis of an uncalibrated threshold. The loop-2 method (proposer–EDA-grounded–criticizer) addresses this by requiring three mechanistically-distinct candidates, a mandatory EDA step that produces ONE concrete number per candidate from train-window DBN ticks before scoring, a critique pass that disqualifies any armchair quantitative parameter, and a final hypothesis structure that names the EDA number behind every numeric setting plus ONE specific result that would falsify the hypothesis in the backtest. If the new method works I'd expect the next reasoning trace to (a) explicitly cite a measured number from the train data — e.g. an empirical trade arrival rate or a conditional-by-side adverse-selection gap — rather than reason from a uniform-density assumption, (b) show evidence of at least one candidate being killed by EDA (visible in NOTES.md → EDA Findings), and (c) state a concrete falsifier the researcher can check against the realized metrics.
